text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Rains and floods caused the death of one person and damaged households and cropland in ten counties.
- IMF's chief negotiatior for Romania, Poul Thomsen, is quoted as saying talks with the country's government had been "useful".
- Romania's health sector is threatened by an acute shortage of funds.
- The SNCFR railway authority and Regia autonoma a huilei hard coal authority top the list of bad debtors to the state budget, the paper says.
- The new Romanian Oil Society will group three refineries.
- Forecasts for coming days announce rains and floods.
- Industry Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu blames the trade unions for delays in implementing reforms.
- Drivers' trade unions plan series of rallies across the country to protest against the new road tax.
- Rains in recent days affected ten counties in western and eastern Romania.
- Romania's national currency will remain stable despite its depreciation in recent days, the paper says.
- A new bill needed to restructure the state airline Tarom awaits the Finance Ministry's endorsement.
